title: Dishonoured Payments, Returned-Payment Fee and Certified-Funds Restriction (Kestrel Advantage Balloon)
content:
**Reversal.** When the payer's bank dishonours a posted payment on a Kestrel Advantage Balloon Retail Installment Sale Contract, the whole payment is reversed against the payment it dishonours, restoring the interest, principal and fee portions it had paid. A returned payment re-opens the installment it had paid; late charges on that installment follow the late charge rule.

**Fee.** A returned-payment fee equal to the lower of the tier's company returned-payment fee and the contract's recorded state maximum returned-payment fee is assessed when the bank's return reason is insufficient funds, account closed or stop payment. No fee is assessed for an unauthorized debit or a bank error, and none where the contract's recorded state maximum is 0.00.

**One fee per return.** Only one returned-payment fee may be assessed for the same dishonoured payment. Whether a fee already stands is read from the company's posting history: a returned-payment fee entry linked to that same dishonoured payment.

**Restriction.** When the count of returned payments on the contract dated within the tier's lookback of calendar months ending on today's date, inclusive, reaches the tier's restriction count, autopay is unenrolled and the certified-funds-only date is set to the date the tier's restriction months calendar months after the latest return date.

## Fee by return reason

| Bank's return reason | Returned-payment fee |
|---|---|
| Insufficient funds, account closed, stop payment | Lower of the company fee and the recorded state maximum |
| Unauthorized debit, bank error | None |
| Any reason, state maximum recorded as 0.00 | None |

## Hypothetical cases

- A company fee of USD 25.00 and a recorded state maximum of USD 15.00 give a fee of USD 15.00 on a stop-payment return.
- A second request to assess a fee on a payment that already carries a returned-payment fee entry is not granted.
